Source format: Committee Charter

2.1 The purpose of the Committee is to protect the integrity of MDOM's online marketplaces and to safeguard the interests of buyers, sellers, and the broader community by:

(a) ensuring that trust and safety risks are identified, assessed, and managed effectively;
(b) promoting transparency and accountability in the handling of safety incidents;
(c) fostering a culture of safety and ethical conduct among marketplace participants; and
(d) advising the MDOM Board on emerging risks and best practice in online marketplace governance.

2.2 In fulfilling its purpose, the Committee shall have due regard to applicable laws of the Commonwealth of Australia and the State of Victoria, including the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth), the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), and the Online Safety Act 2021 (Cth).

**3. Definitions**

3.1 In this Charter, unless the context otherwise requires:

"Board" means the MDOM Board of Directors;

"MDOM" means Maroondah District Online Marketplaces Pty Ltd (ACN 123 456 789);

"Marketplace" means any online platform operated by MDOM, including but not limited to Maroondah Market, Maroondah Trade, and Maroondah Collective;

"Member" means a member of the Committee appointed under section 4;

"Chair" means the Chair of the Committee appointed under section 4.3.

**4. Membership Composition**

4.1 The Committee shall consist of no fewer than seven (7) and no more than eleven (11) members, appointed by the MDOM Board.

4.2 As amended by MMTSC Res. 2022-02, the membership composition shall be as follows:

(a) one (1) member of the MDOM Board, who shall be appointed as Chair;
(b) the MDOM Chief Executive Officer or their nominee;
(c) the MDOM Chief Technology Officer or their nominee;
(d) the Head of Trust & Safety (or equivalent senior executive);
(e) the Head of Legal & Compliance (or equivalent senior executive);
(f) two (2) independent members with relevant expertise in online safety, consumer protection, cybersecurity, or a related field;
(g) up to three (3) additional members appointed at the discretion of the Board, who may include representatives of seller communities, buyer advocacy groups, or academic institutions.

4.3 The Chair shall be appointed by the MDOM Board from among the Board members serving on the Committee. The Chair shall preside over all meetings of the Committee and shall have a casting vote in the event of a tie.

4.4 Members shall be appointed for a term of two (2) years, renewable at the discretion of the Board. Appointments shall be made by written notice from the Board to the Committee.

4.5 A member may resign at any time by written notice to the Chair. The Board may remove a member at any time for cause, including but not limited to conflict of interest, misconduct, or failure to attend three consecutive meetings without reasonable excuse.

4.6 The Committee may, with the approval of the Board, co-opt additional persons to attend meetings in an advisory capacity. Co-opted persons shall not be entitled to vote.

**5. Roles and Responsibilities of Members**

5.1 All members are expected to:

(a) attend meetings regularly and participate constructively;
(b) bring relevant expertise and experience to the Committee's deliberations;
(c) declare any actual or potential conflicts of interest and recuse themselves from related discussions and decisions;
(d) maintain confidentiality of all non-public information received in the course of their duties; and
(e) contribute to the development and review of trust and safety policies.

5.2 The Chair is responsible for:

(a) setting the agenda for each meeting, in consultation with the Secretariat;
(b) ensuring that meetings are conducted efficiently and in accordance with this Charter;
(c) facilitating open and respectful discussion;
(d) reporting to the MDOM Board on the Committee's activities and recommendations; and
(e) representing the Committee in external engagements, as appropriate.
(a) the meeting shall be adjourned to the same day in the following week, at the same time and place; and

(b) if a quorum is not present at the adjourned meeting, the members present may proceed with the business specified in the notice of the original meeting, provided that no resolution on a matter of policy shall be passed unless at least three (3) members are present.

6.6 The Chair shall preside at every meeting of the Committee. In the absence of the Chair, the members present shall elect one of their number to preside at that meeting. The person presiding shall have a casting vote in the event of a tie.

**7. Decision-Making**

7.1 Decisions of the Committee shall be made by a majority of votes of the members present and voting at a meeting at which a quorum is present. Each member shall have one (1) vote.

7.2 The Chair, or the member presiding, shall have a deliberative vote and, in the event of an equality of votes, a casting vote.

7.3 A member with a material personal interest in a matter being considered by the Committee shall:

(a) declare that interest at the meeting, or as soon as practicable after becoming aware of the interest;

(b) not vote on the matter; and

(c) absent themselves from the room during any discussion and decision on the matter, unless the Committee determines otherwise.

7.4 The Committee may decide a matter by circular resolution in writing signed by all members entitled to vote on the matter. A circular resolution is valid and effective as if it had been passed at a meeting of the Committee.

7.5 The Committee may from time to time establish working groups or subcommittees to consider specific matters. The establishment, terms of reference, and membership of any such group shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting at which it is established.

7.6 The Committee shall report to the MDOM Board after each meeting, and shall provide an annual report to the Board on its activities and recommendations during the preceding financial year.

**8. Subcommittees and Reporting Lines**

8.1 The Committee may establish standing subcommittees to assist it in carrying out its functions. Standing subcommittees shall be established by resolution of the Committee and shall operate in accordance with terms of reference approved by the Committee.

8.2 Without limiting the generality of section 8.1, the Committee may establish the following standing subcommittees:

(a) the Policy Review Subcommittee, to review and propose amendments to marketplace trust and safety policies;

(b) the Incident Review Subcommittee, to review serious or systemic trust and safety incidents and report on lessons learned; and

(c) the Metrics and Reporting Subcommittee, to oversee the development and reporting of trust and safety performance indicators.

8.3 Each subcommittee shall have a Chair appointed by the Committee and shall report to the Committee at each ordinary meeting. Subcommittees shall not make decisions on behalf of the Committee unless expressly authorised by the Committee.

8.4 The Committee shall establish reporting lines to ensure that:

(a) the Committee reports to the MDOM Board on all matters of significant risk or material non-compliance with trust and safety policies;

(b) the Chief Trust and Safety Officer, or their delegate, reports to the Committee on operational matters relating to trust and safety, including incident response and policy enforcement; and

(c) the Committee liaises with other committees of the Board, including the Audit and Risk Committee, on matters of shared concern.

8.5 The Committee shall review its own performance and this Charter at least once every two (2) years, and shall recommend any amendments to the MDOM Board for approval.

**9. Amendment of Charter**

9.1 This Charter may be amended by resolution of the MDOM Board, after receiving a recommendation from the Committee.

9.2 Amendments shall be recorded in the minutes of the Committee and the Board, and shall take effect from the date of the Board resolution unless otherwise specified.
**Charter of the Maroondah Marketplaces Trust & Safety Committee**

**10. Membership and Appointment**

10.1 The Committee shall consist of no fewer than five (5) and no more than nine (9) members, appointed by the MDOM Board. Members shall be chosen on the basis of relevant expertise in online marketplace operations, consumer protection, legal compliance, data privacy, or related fields.

10.2 The MDOM Board shall appoint the Chair of the Committee from among its members. The Chair shall be a member of the MDOM Board. The Board may also appoint a Deputy Chair from among the Committee members.

10.3 Members of the Committee shall be appointed for a term of two (2) years, renewable at the discretion of the MDOM Board. Terms shall be staggered so that no more than half of the Committee membership changes in any single year.

10.4 In appointing members, the MDOM Board shall have regard to the need for the Committee to include at least one member with experience in consumer advocacy, at least one member with experience in data security or information technology, and at least one member who is independent of the day-to-day management of Maroondah Digital Online Markets Pty Ltd (MDOM).

10.5 A member may resign at any time by written notice to the Chair and the Company Secretary. A casual vacancy shall be filled by the MDOM Board as soon as practicable, and a member appointed to fill a casual vacancy shall hold office for the remainder of the vacating member's term.

10.6 The MDOM Board may remove a member from the Committee at any time by resolution, provided that the Board has first given the member an opportunity to make written representations to the Board. Removal shall take effect from the date specified in the Board resolution.

10.7 A person ceases to be a member of the Committee if they:
(a) resign in writing to the Chair;
(b) are removed by the MDOM Board under section 10.6;
(c) are absent from three (3) consecutive ordinary meetings of the Committee without leave having been granted by the Committee;
(d) become bankrupt, insolvent, or enter into a scheme of arrangement with creditors;
(e) are convicted of an offence involving dishonesty; or
(f) otherwise become ineligible to act as a member under applicable law.

10.8 The Committee shall notify the MDOM Board in writing as soon as practicable after a member ceases to hold office for any reason.

**11. Meetings and Procedure**

11.1 The Committee shall meet at least six (6) times per calendar year, and at such additional times as the Chair may determine. Meetings may be held in person, by telephone, by video conference, or by a combination of these means.

11.2 The Chair shall preside at all meetings of the Committee at which they are present. If the Chair is absent, the Deputy Chair shall preside. If both are absent, the members present shall elect one of their number to preside at that meeting.

11.3 A quorum shall be a majority of the members of the Committee holding office at the time of the meeting. A meeting may not proceed to business unless a quorum is present.

11.4 Each member present at a meeting shall have one vote. Unless otherwise provided in this Charter, questions arising at a meeting shall be decided by a majority of votes of members present and voting.

11.5 The Chair shall have a deliberative vote only. In the event of an equality of votes, the question shall be deemed to have been lost.

11.6 Minutes of each meeting shall be kept by the Company Secretary or their nominee, and shall be circulated to all members of the Committee within ten (10) business days of the meeting. Minutes shall be confirmed at the next ordinary meeting of the Committee.

11.7 The Committee may invite any employee of MDOM, or any external adviser, to attend all or part of a meeting for the purpose of assisting the Committee in its deliberations. Invitees shall not have a vote.

11.8 Resolutions may be passed by the Committee without a meeting if all members entitled to vote on the resolution have signed a document containing a statement that they are in favour of the resolution, in accordance with the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth) and the MDOM Constitution. A resolution passed in this manner shall be recorded in the minutes of the next ordinary meeting.

## 12. Conflicts of Interest

12.1 A member of the Committee shall, at the time of their appointment, disclose to the Committee any interest, pecuniary or otherwise, that could reasonably be perceived to conflict with the proper performance of their duties as a member. Such disclosures shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting at which they are made.

12.2 Where a member has a material personal interest in a matter before the Committee, the member shall:

(a) declare the nature and extent of the interest prior to discussion of the matter;

(b) absent themselves from the room during discussion and voting on the matter unless the Committee otherwise resolves; and

(c) not vote on the matter.

12.3 The Chair may determine, in consultation with the other members, whether an interest declared under clause 12.2 is material for the purposes of this clause. In making that determination, the Chair shall have regard to the nature of the interest and the likelihood that it could influence the member's conduct in relation to the matter.

12.4 A member who has a continuing interest in a matter may, with the approval of the Committee, make a standing declaration under this clause. A standing declaration shall be reviewed at least annually and may be revoked at any time by the member or by resolution of the Committee.

12.5 The Committee shall maintain a Register of Interests, which shall be kept by the Company Secretary and made available for inspection by the MDOM Board upon request. The Register shall record all disclosures made under this clause, including the date of disclosure and the nature of the interest.

12.6 Nothing in this clause prevents the Committee from seeking the advice of an external adviser who has an interest in a matter, provided that the adviser's interest is disclosed to the Committee and the adviser does not participate in any decision of the Committee on the matter.

---

## 13. Confidentiality

13.1 All members, invitees, and advisers attending meetings of the Committee shall treat as confidential all information received in connection with the business of the Committee, including:

(a) matters relating to the safety and security of users of the MDOM marketplaces;

(b) information concerning investigations into reported incidents;

(c) commercially sensitive information relating to MDOM's operations, partners, or vendors;

(d) personal information of users, sellers, or other persons; and

(e) any other information marked as confidential or which a reasonable person would understand to be confidential.

13.2 The obligation of confidentiality under clause 13.1 does not apply to:

(a) information that is or becomes publicly available other than through a breach of this clause;

(b) information required to be disclosed by law or by a regulatory authority;

(c) information disclosed to the MDOM Board, MDOM's internal audit function, or MDOM's external auditors; or

(d) information disclosed to a law enforcement agency or other government authority in connection with an investigation into a matter within the Committee's remit.

13.3 A member who wishes to disclose confidential information to a third party for a purpose connected with the Committee's work shall first obtain the approval of the Chair. The Chair may impose conditions on any such disclosure, including requirements relating to the protection of personal information.

13.4 The confidentiality obligations in this clause survive the cessation of a person's membership of the Committee.

---

## 14. Relationship with External Agencies

14.1 The Committee may, from time to time, liaise with government agencies, law enforcement bodies, consumer protection authorities, industry bodies, and other organisations for the purpose of advancing the safety and integrity of the MDOM marketplaces.

14.2 Liaison under clause 14.1 shall be conducted in accordance with any applicable privacy laws and with MDOM's Privacy Policy, and shall be subject to the confidentiality obligations in clause 13.

**4. SELLER VERIFICATION PILOT – PHASE 1 REPORT**

P. Dimitriou (Board liaison) joined the meeting for this item.

L. Harrison presented the Phase 1 report for the seller verification pilot, which commenced 1 September 2024. The pilot covers new seller registrations in the home and garden category.

Key points from the report:

- 214 new seller applications were received in the pilot period (1 Sep – 30 Nov).
- Of these, 189 (88.3%) completed the verification steps within the required 5 business days.
- 25 applications (11.7%) did not complete verification and were placed in a pending state. Of these, 12 were later closed due to inactivity after 14 days.
- No seller was allowed to list items until verification was complete.

Discussion:

- M. Petrova asked whether the 14-day closure rule was too short for some sellers, particularly those who may have connectivity issues. L. Harrison confirmed that sellers can reapply at any time, and that the closure is automatic only after 14 days of no contact.
- R. Singh noted that the pilot's completion rate was above the 85% target set in the plan. He asked whether the committee should consider expanding the pilot to another category before the scheduled end date of 31 January 2025. The chairperson noted that this would be a matter for the Board, and that the committee should first see the full evaluation in January.

Decision:

- Motion: That the committee receive and note the Phase 1 report.
- Moved: L. Harrison
- Seconded: R. Singh
- **Carried.**

This volume is the official tally of individual member votes on formal motions put before the Maroondah Marketplaces Trust & Safety Committee (MMTSC) from the commencement of the 2019 sitting year to the present. Each entry records the motion reference, the date of the vote, the quorum observed, and the vote cast by each member present. Votes are recorded as Y (Yes), N (No), or A (Abstain). A member who is absent from a meeting is marked as Absent and no vote is attributed to them. Where a member is present but does not vote for reasons of conflict of interest, this is noted in the remarks column.

The Committee’s quorum is set at five (5) voting members. A motion is carried if it receives a majority of the votes cast, excluding abstentions. The Secretary is responsible for the accuracy of this record and for noting any corrections raised by members at subsequent meetings. Corrections, when made, are entered as a footnote to the original entry and dated.

This volume is a public record of the Committee. It is tabled at each Annual General Meeting and is available for inspection by members of the Maroondah Marketplaces community upon request to the Secretary.

7.5 The Committee may from time to time establish working groups or subcommittees to consider specific matters. The establishment, terms of reference, and membership of any such group shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting at which it is established.

**Charter of the Maroondah Marketplaces Trust & Safety Committee**

**10. Membership and Appointment**

10.1 The Committee shall consist of no fewer than five (5) and no more than nine (9) members, appointed by the MDOM Board. Members shall be chosen on the basis of relevant expertise in online marketplace operations, consumer protection, legal compliance, data privacy, or related fields.

10.2 The MDOM Board shall appoint the Chair of the Committee from among its members. The Chair shall be a member of the MDOM Board. The Board may also appoint a Deputy Chair from among the Committee members.

10.3 Members of the Committee shall be appointed for a term of two (2) years, renewable at the discretion of the MDOM Board. Terms shall be staggered so that no more than half of the Committee membership changes in any single year.

10.4 In appointing members, the MDOM Board shall have regard to the need for the Committee to include at least one member with experience in consumer advocacy, at least one member with experience in data security or information technology, and at least one member who is independent of the day-to-day management of Maroondah Digital Online Markets Pty Ltd (MDOM).

10.5 A member may resign at any time by written notice to the Chair and the Company Secretary. A casual vacancy shall be filled by the MDOM Board as soon as practicable, and a member appointed to fill a casual vacancy shall hold office for the remainder of the vacating member's term.

10.6 The MDOM Board may remove a member from the Committee at any time by resolution, provided that the Board has first given the member an opportunity to make written representations to the Board. Removal shall take effect from the date specified in the Board resolution.

10.7 A person ceases to be a member of the Committee if they:
(a) resign in writing to the Chair;
(b) are removed by the MDOM Board under section 10.6;
(c) are absent from three (3) consecutive ordinary meetings of the Committee without leave having been granted by the Committee;
(d) become bankrupt, insolvent, or enter into a scheme of arrangement with creditors;
(e) are convicted of an offence involving dishonesty; or
(f) otherwise become ineligible to act as a member under applicable law.

10.8 The Committee shall notify the MDOM Board in writing as soon as practicable after a member ceases to hold office for any reason.

**11. Meetings and Procedure**

11.1 The Committee shall meet at least six (6) times per calendar year, and at such additional times as the Chair may determine. Meetings may be held in person, by telephone, by video conference, or by a combination of these means.

11.2 The Chair shall preside at all meetings of the Committee at which they are present. If the Chair is absent, the Deputy Chair shall preside. If both are absent, the members present shall elect one of their number to preside at that meeting.

11.3 A quorum shall be a majority of the members of the Committee holding office at the time of the meeting. A meeting may not proceed to business unless a quorum is present.

11.4 Each member present at a meeting shall have one vote. Unless otherwise provided in this Charter, questions arising at a meeting shall be decided by a majority of votes of members present and voting.

11.5 The Chair shall have a deliberative vote only. In the event of an equality of votes, the question shall be deemed to have been lost.

11.6 Minutes of each meeting shall be kept by the Company Secretary or their nominee, and shall be circulated to all members of the Committee within ten (10) business days of the meeting. Minutes shall be confirmed at the next ordinary meeting of the Committee.

11.7 The Committee may invite any employee of MDOM, or any external adviser, to attend all or part of a meeting for the purpose of assisting the Committee in its deliberations. Invitees shall not have a vote.

11.8 Resolutions may be passed by the Committee without a meeting if all members entitled to vote on the resolution have signed a document containing a statement that they are in favour of the resolution, in accordance with the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth) and the MDOM Constitution. A resolution passed in this manner shall be recorded in the minutes of the next ordinary meeting.

documents.content:
# Charter of the Maroondah Marketplaces Trust & Safety Committee

---

## 12. Conflicts of Interest

12.1 A member of the Committee shall, at the time of their appointment, disclose to the Committee any interest, pecuniary or otherwise, that could reasonably be perceived to conflict with the proper performance of their duties as a member. Such disclosures shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting at which they are made.

12.2 Where a member has a material personal interest in a matter before the Committee, the member shall:

(a) declare the nature and extent of the interest prior to discussion of the matter;

(b) absent themselves from the room during discussion and voting on the matter unless the Committee otherwise resolves; and

(c) not vote on the matter.

12.3 The Chair may determine, in consultation with the other members, whether an interest declared under clause 12.2 is material for the purposes of this clause. In making that determination, the Chair shall have regard to the nature of the interest and the likelihood that it could influence the member's conduct in relation to the matter.

12.4 A member who has a continuing interest in a matter may, with the approval of the Committee, make a standing declaration under this clause. A standing declaration shall be reviewed at least annually and may be revoked at any time by the member or by resolution of the Committee.

12.5 The Committee shall maintain a Register of Interests, which shall be kept by the Company Secretary and made available for inspection by the MDOM Board upon request. The Register shall record all disclosures made under this clause, including the date of disclosure and the nature of the interest.

12.6 Nothing in this clause prevents the Committee from seeking the advice of an external adviser who has an interest in a matter, provided that the adviser's interest is disclosed to the Committee and the adviser does not participate in any decision of the Committee on the matter.

---

## 13. Confidentiality

13.1 All members, invitees, and advisers attending meetings of the Committee shall treat as confidential all information received in connection with the business of the Committee, including:

(a) matters relating to the safety and security of users of the MDOM marketplaces;

(b) information concerning investigations into reported incidents;

(c) commercially sensitive information relating to MDOM's operations, partners, or vendors;

(d) personal information of users, sellers, or other persons; and

(e) any other information marked as confidential or which a reasonable person would understand to be confidential.

13.2 The obligation of confidentiality under clause 13.1 does not apply to:

(a) information that is or becomes publicly available other than through a breach of this clause;

(b) information required to be disclosed by law or by a regulatory authority;

(c) information disclosed to the MDOM Board, MDOM's internal audit function, or MDOM's external auditors; or

(d) information disclosed to a law enforcement agency or other government authority in connection with an investigation into a matter within the Committee's remit.

13.3 A member who wishes to disclose confidential information to a third party for a purpose connected with the Committee's work shall first obtain the approval of the Chair. The Chair may impose conditions on any such disclosure, including requirements relating to the protection of personal information.

13.4 The confidentiality obligations in this clause survive the cessation of a person's membership of the Committee.

---

## 14. Relationship with External Agencies

14.1 The Committee may, from time to time, liaise with government agencies, law enforcement bodies, consumer protection authorities, industry bodies, and other organisations for the purpose of advancing the safety and integrity of the MDOM marketplaces.

14.2 Liaison under clause 14.1 shall be conducted in accordance with any applicable privacy laws and with MDOM's Privacy Policy, and shall be subject to the confidentiality obligations in clause 13.
